title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): a group G with a normal subgroup 𝔊, so that G/𝔊 = Γ. In the Longue Marche context, 𝔊 is the geometric fundamental group, G the arithmetic one, and Γ the Galois group. 'Situation (1)': a homomorphism φ_N : N → G whose composite N → Γ is surjective, with SN := φ_N^{-1}(𝔊). 'Situation (2)': abstract data (𝔊, N, SN ⊲ N, φ_SN : SN → 𝔊, Θ : N → Aut(𝔊)) satisfying condition (3). (3a): for u ∈ SN, Θ(u) = Inn(φ(u)). (3b): φ(aua^{-1}) = Θ(a)(φ(u)), i.e. φ is N-equivariant. In modern terms, (φ, Θ) is a morphism of crossed modules from (SN ↪ N) to (𝔊 → Aut 𝔊).

Reconstruction of G from situation (2):
- Form S_0G = 𝔊 ⋊_Θ N.
- Define i : SN → S_0G by u ↦ u·φ(u)^{-1}. This is a homomorphism (checked on the previous page).
- Its image is normalized by N, by (3b). This page adds that i(u) = uφ(u)^{-1} acts trivially on 𝔊, which is immediate from (3a). Hence i(SN) is normal and centralizes 𝔊.
- Define (6) G := S_0G / i(SN). This gives the commutative square (7): SN ↪ N →φ_N G and SN →φ_SN 𝔊 ↪ G.
- 𝔊 injects into G as a normal subgroup.
- (8) N/SN ≅ G/𝔊.
- (9) Ker(φ_SN) ≅ Ker(φ_N). Hence (10) φ_N is injective iff φ_SN is injective.

Grothendieck concludes that the constructions give mutually inverse equivalences of categories between situations (1) and (2), with a marginal query '(2-cat.?)'.

This is precisely the pushout of the group extension 1 → SN → N → N/SN → 1 along the crossed-module morphism SN → 𝔊, yielding an extension 1 → 𝔊 → G → Γ → 1. The purpose is to describe the arithmetic π1 (or its subgroups generated by 'local' groups N_i, e.g. decomposition/inertia-type subgroups at boundary strata) by geometric data plus Γ-actions. The next page generalizes this to several N_i and a 'relative amalgamated sum' over 𝔊.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. All claims check: the image of 𝔊 is normal; (1,x) = (v, φ(v)^{-1}) forces v = 1 and x = 1, so 𝔊 injects; u ↦ 1 in G iff u ∈ SN and φ(u) = 1, giving the kernel isomorphism (9) and the equivalence (10).
On the previous page S_0G is called a 'produit direct'. It must be the semidirect product 𝔊 ⋊_Θ N, as the formula (*) used there shows.

The equivalence-of-categories claim needs morphisms to be specified (and possibly a 2-categorical structure if G is taken up to inner automorphisms by 𝔊). Grothendieck himself flags this with '(2-cat.?)'; it is left unchecked.

ideas.what: Reconstructing G as (𝔊 ⋊ N)/{u φ(u)^{-1} : u ∈ SN} from a compatible pair (φ : SN → 𝔊, Θ : N → Aut 𝔊)
ideas.modern_name: Pushout of a group extension along a morphism of crossed modules (nonabelian extension theory)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Schreier / Eilenberg–MacLane (nonabelian extensions); Dedecker, Brown–Higgins (crossed modules); Giraud (nonabelian cohomology)
ideas.where_published: Closely related material on extensions and nonabelian cohomology appears in SGA 1 / SGA 7 style discussions and in Giraud's book; exact statement unsure

ideas.what: Equivalence between 'situations' (φ_N : N → G with N ↠ G/𝔊) and abstract data (N, SN, φ_SN, Θ), with injectivity of φ_N equivalent to injectivity of φ_SN
ideas.modern_name: Equivalence between extensions of Γ by 𝔊 induced from N and crossed-module morphisms (SN → N) → (𝔊 → Aut 𝔊)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard folklore in nonabelian group cohomology

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks whether the correspondence should be an equivalence of 2-categories rather than categories. On the following page he extends it to a 'relative amalgamated sum' of several local groups N_i over 𝔊, aimed at reconstructing the arithmetic fundamental group from the geometric one plus local pieces. The single-N case here is standard; the multi-N amalgam is only begun on the next page.
missed.quote: On trouve ainsi des équivalences de catégories (2-cat.?) inverses l'une de l'autre
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. The 2-categorical refinement is now standard (butterflies, crossed-module bicategories), so this page itself adds nothing new.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine nonabelian extension theory (pushout of an extension along a crossed-module morphism), correctly worked out. It is only of interest as a preparatory lemma for the 'relative amalgamated sum' on the next page.
transcription_corrections: 'u quasi induit' should read 'u φ(u)^{-1} induit l'opération triviale sur 𝔊'.
'S∘G' in (6) should read 'S_0G' (the semidirect product 𝔊 ⋊ N), so (6) is G := S_0G / i(SN).
The label (6) duplicates the (6) on the previous page; this is Grothendieck's own numbering.
In diagram (7), SN → N and 𝔊 → G are drawn with hook arrows (inclusions).
The marginal '{2-cat.?}' is attached to 'équivalences de catégories'.
